review_items.rationale: Reviewed fixed plan and assurance_generated_test.go under direct-checks/7736ac8bd1834af584d0f14df7375acf together with execution d686bc84b11b41479b42297a35cca17a stdout and checker result. C_snapshot_campaign_barrier is an implementation_semantics responsibility: the campaign declaration requires legitimate admission, and hup/promotable make pending snapshot presence an explicit exclusion. This does not import a general safety theorem. The actual history uses three bootstrapped RawNodes, completed configuration application, real election and normal proposals; snapshot index 7/term 2 is created from actual application data, whereas recipient storage ends at 5. Actual rejection processing after compaction causes automatic snapshot delivery; the queued snapshot work establishes full restore rather than matching-prefix fast-forward. The caller preserves FIFO local work, does not skip the snapshot head, installs snapshot state only after old normal application, and releases actual attached responses after storage completion. The observer uses public BasicStatus immediately before/after each serialized Campaign call; no intervening network delivery can explain a term change. The completion oracle is an independent driver ledger set after matching snapshot response delivery, not the implementation guard being tested. All three campaign_input prerequisites and results have unique request/phase/node/snapshot_index identities; each call_completed result is observed, with no outcome-dependent filtering. The first two results are follower/term 2 with snapshot_completed false, at applied indexes 4 and 5 respectively. After installation and matching response, the third result is candidate/term 3 with applied 7 and snapshot_completed true. The final fixed drain finishes and observes leader/term 3. The necessary-condition implication holds in this history; the permitted control is observed without strengthening the duty into guaranteed election success. No issue found within this fixed scope. Considered alternatives: The explicit promotable guard and snapshot-specific completion path explain the observed held-work branches. They do not establish every restore history. Campaign documentation says it causes a candidate transition, but actual Step admission may ignore the request. The checker correctly observes role/term rather than treating a nil return as admission. The original exploration failed before snapshot fallback because its scheduler held rejection replies. The fixed formal artifact permits earlier FIFO work and reached the full-restore prerequisite; no result from that failed exploration is attributed to this check.
limitations: One full snapshot and older normal-entry application batch, fixed voters and no independent term transition; no replacement snapshot, restart or stale-term completion comparison.
The requirement is locally source-defined campaign eligibility, not proof of overall consensus safety or client-visible correctness.
Older configuration application against snapshot-installed membership remains a distinct unresolved caller-contract question.
